decisions.reason: Although this chamber may overlap with other models, four years of survival in a core dosimetry category suggests performance has likely stayed near aspiration levels, so we keep it unless clearer evidence of cannibalisation or weak demand appears.

This standard clinical ionization chamber line sits squarely in our core business and likely benefits from stable benchmark demand and service complementarities, making withdrawal within a year unlikely.
As a specialist relative-dosimetry chamber it probably serves a narrower segment, but it remains closely tied to our competence base and is worth keeping while it supports the broader QA portfolio.
A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional, core-adjacent product with modest uncertainty and good fit to our installed base, so organizational slack and portfolio logic favor retention.
